checks: The standard simplex centroid is g by the average of its d+1 vertices, hence K is centroid zero and the middle centroid is −δv. Since v∈K, the two identical continuous endpoints ρK lie in the proposed middle by convexity. Every hull point therefore has its continuous coordinate in the proposed middle. The base projection is exactly [−1,1], endpoint bases are exposed, and the displayed middle is present by construction. This proves the full integer census and d+1-dimensionality.
In tK the sum inequality for −δv is dδ/(d+1)≤t/(d+1); the lower coordinate inequalities hold for all t≥0. Thus γ_K(−δv)=dδ, including δ=0.

The affine form λ(x)=1/(d+1)−Σ_i x_i/ρ equals one at ρv and zero at all other vertices of ρK, so it is the specified barycentric coordinate. Its value at the actual middle centroid is a. The halfspace λ(x)≤a(1+z) is proper and contains that mark on its boundary, with thresholds zero at −1 and 2a at 1.

For λ≥t with 0≤t≤1 the endpoint region is tρv+(1−t)ρK, by barycentric coordinates. Its volume is (1−t)^dρ^dV, and all boundary levels have zero d-volume. Since 2a∈[0,1], the second endpoint contributes the complementary volume at 2a, while the first only contributes the opposite facet. The boundary t=1 occurs at d=1, δ=0 and gives the entire second endpoint under the sublevel inequality, as the formula states.

At δ=ρ/d the two thresholds are zero, and the cap is Σ_i x_i≥ρ/(d+1). It captures only facets in both endpoints, giving zero volume. For any real D<d the proposed coefficient produces 1−Dδ/ρ=1−D/d>0, contradicting the zero pair mass for any positive equal-pair budget. The cap expression is the mass of this explicit cap for the stated δ range.

Independently checked the gauge, barycentric threshold and cap polynomial with exact rational arithmetic for dimensions 1–12 and sampled rational scales and offsets, including both offset endpoints. The homothety and gauge arguments establish the formulas for every dimension and scale.

overlap.comparison: The accepted simplex argument establishes first-order sharpness of a projected centroid displacement with respect to a missing-volume fraction, using truncated source simplices. This example instead has three homothetic fibers and proves exact sharpness of a radius-surplus coefficient for the endpoint cap budget at the actual own centroid.

Its sharp example stretches one vertex of a containing simplex and places its centroid on a facet of a contained simplex at volume ratio 2. At d=1 this coincides up to affine coordinates with the endpoint-collapse geometry here. For d≥2 the present larger simplex is a translated homothet, has volume ratio (1+1/d)^d at collapse, and supplies the exact Minkowski gauge and tilted endpoint-volume branch.
For equal radii its positive pair budget is at the midpoint of the endpoint centroids, which is zero here. The zero cap in this example is at the displaced actual middle centroid.

readability: The symbol v denotes a simplex vertex, while V denotes the d-dimensional volume. The coefficient obstruction concerns the paired endpoint portion of a halfspace, and the proof is independent of the separate positive-budget candidate.

summary: The full-dimensional three-fiber simplex hull realizes the sharp displacement dδ. At δ=ρ/d the through-centroid supporting cap has zero endpoint volume, and the explicit cap branch has the asserted exact mass.
